full_judgment:
5. Mr. Moudud Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf the opposite parties, on the other hand, by filing counter affidavit opposes the Rule. He submits that the explanation for delay as stated in the application is totally false inasmuch as the petitioners in the application for condonation of delay stated that the Government pleader filed several applications for certified copies of the judgment and decree dated 26.02.2009 (decree signed on 01.3.2009) passed by the learned District Judge, Narayangonj in Title Appeal No.90 of 2008 on 10.3.2009, 8.5.2009, 10.8.2009 and 13.11.2009 respectively but those applications were rejected as the record of the case was not sent to Nokolkharia but the information slip dated 01.7.2014 as contained in "Annexure-X" to the counter affidavit shows that petitioners did not file any application on 27.02.2009, 10.3.2009, 8.5.2009, 10.8.2003 and 13.11. 2009 for procuring certified copies before filing the application on 15.01.2013 for procuring certified copies of the judgment and decree dated 26.02.2009. He further submits that in this case the petitioners miserably failed to explain the inordinate delay of 1467 days in filing the revision application and therefore, they are not entitled to get benefit of section 5 of the Limitation Act. Mr. Moudud Ahmed in support of his submission has relied on the decisions reported in 14 MLR 408, 57 DIA 586, 21 BLD 107, 16 OLD 267, 6 BLD(AD)180, 59 DLR(AD) 1, 21 BLD(AD) 35 and 57 DI,R 586. 

 8. As there was delay of 1467 days in filing the revision application before this Court an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act was filed for condonation of delay. It was stated in the application for condonation of delay that the delay may be condoned as there was no willful lathes on the part of the Government for making the delay which was caused due to not sending the case record to Nokolkhana in time and also to obtain opinions of various authorities concerned. 

 9. On a close perusal of the information slip as contained in "Annexure-X" to the counter affidavit, it appears that no application was filed for obtaining certified copies prior to file application dated 15.01.2013 for procuring certified copies of the judgment and decree dated 26.02.2009. The petitioners stated in the application that they tried to get the certified copies of the judgment and decree dated 26.02.2009 by filing number of applications up to 13.11.2009 but they did not explain as to why they kept the matter pending from 14.11.2009 to 15.01.2013, that is, 1157 days. It is really surprising to see that more than 3 years consumed to file application for procuring certified copies of the judgment and decree dated 26.02.2009. The Government Pleader is well aware of the consequence of delay, although for the reasons best known to him as to why after being unsuccessful in all the courts below he took 1157 days for filing an application for condonation of delay and allowed the period of limitation to run out. This is gross negligence on the part of the Government Pleader. Further, it appears that admittedly Government pleader obtained the certified copies on 23.01.2013 and thereafter, more than 5 months consumed to file the revision application on 06.06.2013 in spite of fact that concerned officials are well known that the revision application was already heavily barred by limitation. This indicates that in the instant case they acted in the negligent way.
